note: A single open gravel lot directly beside paved PA 414, about 3 miles south of Slate Run; the agency says the campsite is immediately adjacent to the road. It is the one drive-in site numbered with the Black Walnut Bottom camping area: the area's other sites (BW 001 to 018) are listed by the agency as primitive sites with no trailer access and begin about 140 m to the north-west, towards Pine Creek. Pine Creek is about 150 m away through woods and a meadow and is not in view on imagery. Picnic table; no toilet or water at this site. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: BW 019 still listed and bookable online, Drive-In, 'RV Site' category, max vehicle and equipment length 60 ft, pull-in gravel driveway 164 ft, grades Slight, clearance 50 ft, picnic table; count 1 and 60 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; sells in all five windows. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none at this site. Imagery (Esri, leaf-on): an open gravel lot about 25 x 25 m with a gravel lane looping in from PA 414 at its north-west end, the pin on the lot. Pine Creek: NHD centreline 171 m, bank about 150 m, woods and a meadow between; not waterfront.
flags: BLACK WALNUT BOTTOM: BW 019 carries the area's prefix but is a separate roadside pull-off. DCNR GIS: BW 019 is the only 'Motorized' record (TrailerAccess Yes, Latrines No, 'Formerly PA-414 BWB Pull Off', 'Near Black Walnut Bottom'); BW 001 to BW 018 are Type 'Primitive', TrailerAccess No, Latrines Yes, 140 m (BW 018) to 494 m (BW 013) from BW 019. The Tiadaghton camping page calls Black Walnut Bottom one of the 'State forest rustic campsites', which 'usually include a pit latrine or vault toilet, but no other amenities'. So a latrine exists in the primitive-site area, not at this site; vault_toilets written false for the site itself, on the page's attributes and the GIS 'Latrines: No'.

PINE CREEK RAIL TRAIL / comfort station: not established. No page read places the rail trail or a comfort station at BW 019, and imagery shows only woods and a meadow between the lot and the creek. Not written anywhere.

Water: Pine Creek NHD centreline 171 m and NHD area edge 150 m south-west of the site, with the primitive sites, woods and a meadow between; Riffle Run 190 m. Not waterfront and no view on imagery; no lead.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Site Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Grade: Slight', gravel; on a paved state highway. No caution line on the page. The page also carries the district-wide 'Road and Travel Alert' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' boilerplate (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
NAME: the stored name carries the site's own number and road as the booking system gives them ('Site, Loop: BW 019, PA-414'); nothing to change.

Equestrian/ATV check: the Tiadaghton horseback page names no horse camp; the ATV page names only the Haneyville ATV Trail (trailhead on SR 44 on its brochure map). The 2024 ATV Regional Trail Connector Pilot map linked from the advisories page answered 404 and is UNREAD.

Tiadaghton advisories page (read 2026-11-10): Brown's Run and Sinking Springs Roads closed to snowmobiles with a detour (2024-2025 season); 'Stay alert for ATVs' (ATV pilot uses some PennDOT, township and forest roads); a dust advisory for the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail; Dividing Line Trail closed indefinitely; e-bike rules. No road closure, gate, bridge limit or timber-sale notice on this entry's road. The Tiadaghton camping page publishes no seasonal closure, hunting-season rule or site rotation; it says only 'State forest roads do not receive winter maintenance and are not plowed --motorized, roadside camping access is not guaranteed. Travel at your own risk.'
